Conceptualization: Define the overarching question before any technical design is chosen.
Turn a broad problem into the main scientific hypothesis.
Propose the central idea that motivates the investigation.
Decide the intellectual aims that the research should pursue.
Identify a gap in prior work and frame a new question around it.
Shape the initial direction of the project by proposing its central thesis.
Data curation: Clean inconsistent field values and document the resulting records.
Create a data dictionary so that others can reuse the collected measurements.
Maintain the archived dataset and annotate its missing values.
Merge datasets by stable identifiers and remove duplicate records.
Standardize observation metadata and deposit the curated files.
Organize the raw observations into a documented, reusable dataset.
Formal analysis: Fit a regression model and estimate the uncertainty of its coefficients.
Compute quantitative contrasts between the treatment and reference groups.
Apply an inferential procedure to the observed measurements.
Summarize multiple measurements using an explicit statistical model.
Evaluate mathematical relationships from the observed results.
Estimate effect sizes and perform the planned statistical tests.
Funding acquisition: Secure a grant that pays for the research.
Obtain financial backing for the proposed work.
Win external financial support to carry out the study.
Lead the proposal that brought in research funds.
Arrange sponsorship that finances personnel and research expenses.
Acquire the award that supports the publication's project.
Investigation: Carry out the field measurements called for in the study.
Run the experiments and collect the resulting observations.
Conduct interviews to gather first-hand research evidence.
Collect observations in accordance with the agreed protocol.
Perform the hands-on research procedures and gather primary evidence.
Administer the study procedure and record each participant's observations.
Methodology: Design the procedure to be followed when gathering observations.
Develop the measurement and sampling strategy for the study.
Specify an experimental design with appropriate controls.
Create the model and set out the rules for using it in the study.
Design an approach that translates the research question into measurable outcomes.
Establish the technical protocol used to obtain and interpret results.
Project administration: Coordinate work packages, schedules and project milestones.
Organize meetings and manage the dependencies between research teams.
Track tasks and deadlines for day-to-day project execution.
Arrange the study logistics across participating sites.
Maintain the operational project plan and coordinate handoffs.
Manage delivery dates and organize the allocation of project tasks.
Resources: Provide access to the equipment needed for the study.
Supply materials or instruments for other investigators to use.
Make an existing research collection available to the team.
Contribute access to samples, tools or computing facilities.
Supply an instrument that the research group would otherwise lack.
Provide the specimens and instrumentation used by the investigators.
Software: Write the code that implements the computational pipeline.
Build and maintain the program used by the research team.
Implement the proposed algorithm as executable source code.
Create a software package to process the study inputs.
Develop and debug the scripts that automate the computation.
Program the tool used to run the reported analysis.
Supervision: Provide scientific oversight and mentor the researchers performing the work.
Guide the research team and advise its junior members.
Oversee the direction of the trainees' research activities.
Act as the senior advisor responsible for research oversight.
Provide continuing scientific guidance to the project's investigators.
Mentor the staff conducting the study and review their progress.
Validation: Verify that an independent repeat produces consistent findings.
Check whether reported results can be reproduced with the provided inputs.
Replicate key measurements as a check on the study's conclusions.
Confirm the output agrees with the expected result on independent checks.
Independently verify the computational results by repeating the analysis.
Check the reproducibility of the reported outcome.
Visualization: Prepare the plots that communicate the study's findings.
Draw the figures and diagrams used to present the results.
Create graphical summaries of the evidence for the publication.
Design the visual displays that explain the reported relationships.
Produce charts and organize the figures for readers.
Render the measurements into visual representations for interpretation.
Writing – original draft: Write the initial manuscript text before coauthors revise it.
Prepare the first version of the article narrative.
Draft the manuscript's sections from the study material.
Compose the original text submitted for comments.
Turn the research into an initial written paper.
Write the first complete paper for the research team.
Writing – review & editing: Critically revise an existing manuscript and improve its arguments.
Review the draft and edit its wording before publication.
Incorporate reviewer feedback into the already written article.
Evaluate the manuscript's clarity and revise the existing text.
Make substantive changes to the earlier draft during review.
Edit and critically comment on a manuscript written by the team.
